overclaims: These findings establish a real vulnerability, but do not settle the full cost-and-speed claim.

checks.note: Excerpt, proposition, conditions, axis, horizon and outcome (unresolved) are all correct. Two problems. The limitation that the NATO experiment 'primarily uses non-political scenarios' is not supported by the e2 excerpt or context. 'Establish a real vulnerability' says more than the evidence does and leans toward support while the outcome is unresolved: e1 tests only reader deception, and e2 also records substantial account removals. Citation excerpts, publishers and dates match the items.

Instruction tuning reduced some effects; ingestion and success depend on the pipeline and content.
checks.note: Excerpt, proposition, the condition and the outcome (supported) are all correct. Two factual limitations have no basis in the evidence. 'Models up to 1.3 billion parameters' appears nowhere in e1; the only model size given is Anthropic's 13B in e2. 'Instruction tuning reduced some effects' is also not in any evidence item or explanation. 'Realistic data filtering' slightly overstates e1's description of extraction and filtering. Citations are otherwise accurate.

Excerpt and proposition are faithful. The 'already' qualifier and the target period ending on the post date are visible. Both sources predate the post: e1 (Observer, 2026-01-04) gives the a16z investment, and e2 (Futurism/Yahoo, 2025-10-27) preserves the thousand-account, physical-device and human-mimicry advertising wording. The limitations about the changed website and the partially accessible 404 Media page match the packet. Excerpts, publishers, dates and relations are correct. Axis historical_observation, outcome supported.
